subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Positive Displacement Pumps: Push Every Drop
description: A micro-lesson that makes Positive Displacement Pumps: Push Every Drop usable.

hook.text: Squeeze a tube of toothpaste. That push-and-seal action is a pump.

buildup.text: PD pumps trap a fixed volume and push it forward each cycle.

discovery.text: They deliver steady flow regardless of pressure. Speed sets the rate.

twist.text: Block the outlet and pressure spikes dangerously. A relief valve is vital.

climax.text: Fuel injectors, hydraulic pumps, and metering systems all use PD pumps.

punchline.text: Trap it, squeeze it, push it. Every drop counts.

quiz.question: Why do positive displacement pumps need relief valves?
options: To allow air to enter and prevent vacuum lock
They keep pushing regardless of outlet pressure, risking dangerous spikes
To regulate the speed of the motor driving the pump
